entry.name: MySQL Explain Analyzer
entry.description: A web-based analyzer of `EXPLAIN FORMAT=JSON` output, providing comments, scalability analysis and permalinks for saved samples.
entry.line: - [MySQL Explain Analyzer](https://github.com/Preetam/explain-analyzer) - A web-based analyzer of `EXPLAIN FORMAT=JSON` output, providing comments, scalability analysis and permalinks for saved samples.

evidence.observation: Features: table representation, comments about explain interpretation, experimental scalability analysis, automatic dialect detection. No saving or permalinks. Accepts MySQL `EXPLAIN FORMAT=JSON`.

'remove save button' (2021-07-23) changed js/index.js. Later commits 5e8fa4f and 3f93a06 rewrote the app in Mithril 2/TypeScript with PostgreSQL support. A grep of the current src/ for permalink/save/share/localStorage found no matches.
archived=false, BSD-2-Clause, pushed_at 2026-11-02, description 'MySQL and PostgreSQL JSON Explain Analyzer'.

limitations: Mentioning PostgreSQL support is optional and not needed for accuracy.
I did not run the web app; the absence of the feature comes from the source code and README.
assessment.newDescription: A web-based analyzer of `EXPLAIN FORMAT=JSON` output, providing comments and scalability analysis.
assessment.reason: Identity confirmed: Preetam/explain-analyzer, BSD-2-Clause, active as of 2026-11. The claim about 'permalinks for saved samples' is out of date. Commit 7058205 ('remove save button', 2021-07-23) removed saving. The README Features list in the current modernized release no longer includes 'Explain saving and permalinks', and the current src/ contains no save or permalink code. The other claims still hold: a web-based analyzer of MySQL `EXPLAIN FORMAT=JSON` output, comments, and experimental scalability analysis. PostgreSQL support was added, but listing it is optional.

entry.name: Databasus
entry.description: tool for scheduled MySQL backups via web UI with external storages (local, S3, FTP, Google Drive, etc.), notifications (webhook, Discord, Slack, etc.) and team management.
entry.line: - [Databasus](https://github.com/databasus/databasus) - tool for scheduled MySQL backups via web UI with external storages (local, S3, FTP, Google Drive, etc.), notifications (webhook, Discord, Slack, etc.) and team management.

evidence.observation: Tagline 'PostgreSQL backup tool'. Supported databases: PostgreSQL 14–18 (physical and logical), MySQL 5.7, 8.0, 8.4, 9 and 26 (logical only), MariaDB, MongoDB. Storages: 'S3, Cloudflare R2, Azure Blob Storage, NAS, FTP, SFTP and more'. Notifiers: Email, Telegram, Slack, Discord, Teams, Mattermost, webhooks. Workspaces and access management. No mention of Google Drive.
Supported storages: Local Storage, S3, Cloudflare R2, Azure Blob Storage, NAS, FTP, SFTP. Google Drive is absent.
Includes Azure blob, minio (S3), jlaffaye/ftp and pkg/sftp clients, and go-sql-driver/mysql. There is no google.golang.org/api (Drive) module.
archived=false, Apache-2.0, pushed 2026-11-10, description 'PostgreSQL backup tool with Point-In-Time-Recovery and restore verification'.

limitations: The README says 'and more' after the storage list. Removal of Google Drive is inferred from the official docs list and the dependency manifest; I did not find a changelog entry that announces it.
The project's focus has shifted to PostgreSQL. MySQL support is logical-only but still documented.
I did not run the software.
assessment.newDescription: tool for scheduled MySQL backups via web UI with external storages (local, S3, FTP, etc.), notifications (webhook, Discord, Slack, etc.) and team management.
assessment.reason: databasus/databasus is canonical, Apache-2.0 licensed, and active. The project now positions itself mainly as a PostgreSQL backup tool, but its README still lists MySQL 5.7–9/26 support (logical backups only), so it still fits the Backup section. Scheduled backups, web UI, webhook/Discord/Slack notifications and team features (workspaces, access management) are still documented, and local, S3 and FTP storage are still listed. Google Drive is not: neither the README storage list nor the official Storages docs page (Local, S3, Cloudflare R2, Azure Blob, NAS, FTP, SFTP) mentions it, and backend/go.mod has no Google Drive API dependency. I recommend removing that example; non-exhaustive 'etc.' wording keeps it durable.

entry.name: wtx
entry.description: Client for MySQL/MariaDB/Percona written in Rust
entry.line: - [wtx](https://github.com/c410-f3r/wtx) - Client for MySQL/MariaDB/Percona written in Rust

evidence.observation: Commit 'feat!: Allow the decoding and encoding of arbitrary collections' (2026-05-01, PR #523) removes wtx/src/database/client/mysql.rs, the mysql/ submodule files, wtx-examples/database/database-client-mysql.rs, .scripts/integration-tests-mysql.sh and .test-utils/mysql.sh.
Current manifest (version 0.52.1) defines postgres and postgres-pool features. No mysql, mariadb or percona feature exists. A recursive tree listing of main has no mysql paths.
Database Client docs document only PostgreSQL.

Issue '[MySQL] Add support for MariaDB/MySQL/Percona' was closed 2025-02-23. MySQL support was added around March 2025 (commit 'Add MySQL client') and later removed.

limitations: The removal commit and PR #523 give no reason, and I found no statement on whether MySQL support might return.

assessment.reason: Recommend opening a removal issue, not a patch. The listed project no longer provides the MySQL/MariaDB/Percona client the entry describes. Commit e266e965fb (2026-05-01, PR #523) deleted wtx/src/database/client/mysql*, the MySQL example and the MySQL integration-test scripts. The current wtx/Cargo.toml has only postgres features, and the database-client docs and README cover only PostgreSQL. The project is still active, but its MySQL interface has been removed. Version 0.44.2 still had the mysql feature.

entry.name: Shift
entry.description: An application that helps you run schema migrations on MySQL databases
entry.line: - [Shift](https://github.com/square/shift) - An application that helps you run schema migrations on MySQL databases

blockers: SchemaBot is young (created 2026-04, v0.1.x, a few dozen stars). Whether it meets the list's 'reasonably recognized and adopted' / GA-quality conditions, or should go under Incubating, needs maintainer judgement.

evidence.observation: NOTE block: 'Shift is no longer under active development. Its successor is SchemaBot (https://github.com/block/schemabot), Block's GitOps tool for database schema changes ... Online MySQL schema changes run with Spirit.'
Latest commits: 2026-09-04/08 'Point readers to SchemaBot and Spirit in the README' (merged PR #112). The previous functional commit is from 2020-09.

GitHub API: block/schemabot, not archived, Apache-2.0, created 2026-04-07, pushed 2026-11-10. Description: 'Define your database schema in code and apply changes safely through pull requests or the CLI'.

README badges: 'MySQL: GA', 'Vitess: GA', 'PostgreSQL: early alpha'. Declarative and GitOps-driven: compares SQL files to the live database and applies changes through PRs or a CLI. Releases v0.1.81–v0.1.83 in Oct–Nov 2026.

limitations: SchemaBot is declarative/GitOps, whereas Shift was a UI-driven pt-osc runner. The workflows differ, but the successor relationship is officially stated.
I did not run either tool.
assessment.newDescription: Declarative, GitOps-driven schema change tool for MySQL that plans and applies changes through pull requests or a CLI
assessment.reason: The Shift README now officially states: 'Shift is no longer under active development. Its successor is SchemaBot, Block's GitOps tool for database schema changes', with online MySQL changes run by Spirit. Block is Square's parent company, and the notice was merged into square/shift in 2026-09. The project is therefore officially discontinued, which conflicts with the 'must not be abandoned/discontinued' condition, and it names an official successor. block/schemabot is Apache-2.0, actively released (v0.1.83 on 2026-11-03), and its README badges MySQL support as GA. Because this effectively removes Shift, the change should go through an issue.

findings.previewHold: 0 proposed change(s); 1 held for unresolved questions.

entry.line: - [Percona Replication Manager](https://github.com/percona/replication-manager) - Asynchronous MySQL replication manager agent for Pacemaker. Supports file and GTID based replication, geo-distributed clusters using booth.

evidence.observation: Titled 'Replication manager for PXC and MariaDB'. Manages asynchronous replication between PXC or MariaDB clusters, uses Galera for quorum within a cluster, and states 'This solution works only with GTID based replication'. No mention of Pacemaker or booth.

Canonical nwo percona/replication-manager, not a fork. Files: replication_manager.sh, replication_manager5.sh, percona-replication-manager_builder.sh, debian/, rpm/. Latest commit is dated 2026-01-07.

Redirects to Percona-Lab/pacemaker-replication-agents, described as a 'Repository of the Percona Pacemaker resource agents'. README refers to PRM mailing lists. Agents include mysql_prm and mysql_prm_gtid.

The geo-DR guide mentions booth 26 times. This matches the entry's 'geo-distributed clusters using booth' claim, so the current description belongs to this repo, not the one linked. Its latest commit is dated 2017-03-31.

limitations: Did not run either tool.

The other possible fix, pointing the entry at Percona-Lab/pacemaker-replication-agents and keeping the old description, is also consistent with the evidence, but that repo has had no commits since 2017. The maintainer may prefer that option or opening an issue.
assessment.newDescription: Manages asynchronous GTID replication links between Percona XtraDB Cluster or MariaDB Galera clusters.
assessment.reason: The listed URL works, but the repository it points to is a different tool from the one the entry describes. percona/replication-manager (not a fork) is a shell-script tool that manages asynchronous GTID replication links between Percona XtraDB Cluster or MariaDB Galera clusters. Its README says it works only with GTID-based replication and never mentions Pacemaker or booth. The Pacemaker agent the description refers to (PRM: Pacemaker, file and GTID agents, booth for geo-DR) is a separate repo, Percona-Lab/pacemaker-replication-agents (percona/percona-pacemaker-agents redirects there). That repo's last commit was in 2017. Recommended: keep the URL and correct the description so it matches the repo actually linked.

assessment.reason: The MariaDB/mcp README opens with an official deprecation notice: effective November 3, 2026, the repo is deprecated, and all MariaDB MCP Server development and releases move to mariadb-corporation/ai-plugins.
